citation: X. Zhang, Y. Sugano, M. Fritz, A. Bulling. "It's Written All Over Your Face: Full-Face Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation." CVPR Workshops (CVPRW), 2017.
X. Zhang, Y. Sugano, M. Fritz, A. Bulling. "Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation in the Wild." CVPR, 2015.

eyeos.description: shipping EyeOS: eyeos.calibration.Calibration with its defaults (affine in the 4 iris offsets, ridge 1e-3)

eyeos-poly2.description: eyeos.calibration.Calibration(degree=2): adds squares and pairwise products

per-dot-1.description: shipping calibration fitted on 1 image(s) per calibration dot

per-dot-5.description: shipping calibration fitted on 5 image(s) per calibration dot

per-dot-10.description: shipping calibration fitted on 10 image(s) per calibration dot

per-dot-20.description: shipping calibration fitted on 20 image(s) per calibration dot

with-head-pose.description: experiment: ridge regression (lambda 1e-3, standardised features) on the 4 iris offsets plus EyeOS's yaw, pitch and roll; not part of eyeos/

global-lopo.description: experiment: leave-one-person-out ridge (lambda 1e-3, standardised iris offsets plus head pose -> screen fractions) trained on every other participant, then a per-user affine correction fitted on this participant's 9-dot calibration set

notes.static_photos: MPIIFaceGaze is still photos, not live video, so the One Euro filter, dwell (Gate 3) and click confirmation are not exercised: every error is one frame's calibration output, rounded and clamped to the screen like the cursor pixel.
notes.calibration_set: For each of EyeOS's 9 calibration dots, the K valid images whose true target is nearest the dot stand in for looking at it, and are added with their true targets. calibration_mean_distance_px says how far from the dots those images were.
notes.screens: Each participant's own laptop screen (screenSize.mat) is the screen, not the user's: pixel errors are in that screen's pixels, and % of the diagonal compares across screens.
notes.valid_frames: valid = exactly one face and both irises visible, what Gate 1 needs; detection_rate = valid / images. Invalid frames are in neither the calibration nor the test set.
notes.test_sets: the test set is every valid image not used for calibration, so a variant with more images per dot is tested on slightly fewer images.
notes.angular_error: the angle between (P_pred - fc) and (gt - fc), with the predicted pixel P_pred mapped to camera coordinates by the screen model recorded under screen_model; null for a person whose screen model does not reproduce the annotated gt within the tolerance.
notes.head_pose: EyeOS's own simplified head pose (eyeos.features), not the dataset's: the share of test frames within Gate 2's head-pose limit of the calibration pose.
notes.validation_error_px: Calibration's own leave-one-out RMS error for the eyeos.calibration variants, and the same leave-one-out definition for the other models; Gate 2 passes below the limit.
